## Load the libraries
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(shiny)
library(shinythemes)
library(janitor)
```

Surgery Timing: A dataset from 32,001 elective general surgery patients who were treated at Cleveland Clinic between 2005 and 2010. It is well known that lack of sleep and heavy workloads can negatively affect performance. Hospital staff frequently face these challenges, especially during busier periods. Because of this, researchers wanted to determine whether the time at which surgery is performed has any impact on patient outcomes.


```{r}
surgery <- read_csv("data/surgery.csv") %>% 
  clean_names()
```
1. What are the variable names?
```{r}
names(surgery)
```

2.What is the distribution of patient age and race?
```{r}
surgery %>% 
  filter(race!="NA") %>% 
  group_by(race) %>% 
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    min_age=min(age, na.rm = T),
    max_age=max(age, na.rm = T),
    mean_age = mean(age, na.rm = T),
    median_age = median(age, na.rm = T)
  ) %>% 
  arrange(desc(n))
```


3.At what age do people undergo surgery more? 
```{r}
surgery %>% 
  group_by(age) %>% 
  summarise(
    n = n()
  ) %>% 
  arrange(desc(n))
```
```{r}
surgery %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=age))+
  geom_histogram()+
  labs(title= "Distribution of Surgery by Age",
       x=NULL,
       y="# of Surgery's")
```


4. How many males and females were sampled in this study?
```{r}
surgery %>% 
  filter(gender!="NA") %>% 
  count(gender)
```

```{r}
 surgery %>% 
  filter(gender != "NA") %>% 
  count(gender) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = gender, y = n, fill = gender)) +
  geom_col(fill= "turquoise4", color ="black", alpha = 0.9) +
  labs(title = "Number of Males and Females",
       x = "Gender",
       y = "Count")+
  theme_minimal()
```

5.Is mortality higher in males or females?
```{r}
surgery %>%
  filter(gender != "NA") %>%
  count(gender, mort30)
```

```{r}
surgery %>%
  filter(gender != "NA") %>%
  group_by(gender) %>%
  summarize(mortality = sum(mort30 == "Yes", na.rm = T)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = gender, y = mortality)) +
  geom_col(fill = "turquoise4", color = "black", alpha =0.9) +
  labs(title = "Deaths by Gender",
       x = "Gender",
       y = "Number of Deaths")+
  theme_minimal()
```


6.What month is mortality highest in and what month is the best for surgery?
January has the most deaths, while December has the least.
```{r}
surgery %>%
  filter(month != "NA") %>%
   mutate(month = factor(month, c("Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun","Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec"))) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarize(mortality = sum(mort30 == "Yes", na.rm = T)) %>%
  arrange(month)
```

```{r}
surgery %>%
  filter(month != "NA") %>%
  mutate(month = factor(month, c("Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun","Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec"))) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarize(mortality = sum(mort30 == "Yes", na.rm = T)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = month, y = mortality)) +
  geom_col(fill = "turquoise4", color = "black", alpha = 0.8) +
  theme_minimal()+
  labs(title = "Deaths by Month",
       x = "Month",
       y = "Number of Deaths")
```

7. What complication shows the highest mortality?
```{r}
surgery %>%
  filter(mort30 == "Yes") %>%
  select(baseline_cancer, baseline_cvd, baseline_dementia,
         baseline_diabetes, baseline_digestive,
         baseline_osteoart, baseline_psych,
         baseline_pulmonary) %>%
  summarise_all(~sum(. == "Yes", na.rm = T))
```
```{r}
surgery %>%
  filter(mort30 == "Yes") %>%
  select(baseline_cancer, baseline_cvd, baseline_dementia,
         baseline_diabetes, baseline_digestive,
         baseline_osteoart, baseline_psych,
         baseline_pulmonary) %>%
  summarise_all(~sum(. == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "complication",
               values_to = "deaths") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(complication, deaths), y = deaths)) +
  geom_col(fill= "turquoise4", color ="black", alpha = 0.9) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Deaths by Baseline Complication",
       x = "Complication",
       y = "Number of Deaths")+
  theme_minimal()
```

8.Does ASA status predict mortality?
```{r}
surgery %>%
  filter(asa_status!="NA") %>% 
  group_by(asa_status) %>%
  summarise(mortality_rate = mean(mort30 == "Yes", na.rm = T))
```

```{r}
surgery %>% 
  filter(asa_status != "NA") %>%
  group_by(asa_status) %>% 
  summarize(mortality = sum(mort30 == "Yes", na.rm = T)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = asa_status, y = mortality)) + 
  geom_col(fill = "turquoise4", color = "black", alpha = 0.8) + 
  labs(title = "Death Count Based on ASA Status", x = "ASA Status", y = "Number of Deaths")+ theme_minimal()
```

9.Is there any association between moon phase and mortality?
```{r}
moon <- surgery %>% 
  group_by(moonphase) %>% 
  summarize(
    mortality_rate = mean(mort30 == "Yes", na.rm = T),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop")
```


```{r}
moon %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = moonphase,
             y = mortality_rate,
             group = 1)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    title = "Mortality Rate by Moonphase",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mortality Rate"
  )
```
```{r}
moon2 <- surgery %>%

```

```{r}

```

12.What time is associated with the highest mortality?


15. Create a Shiny App...
```{r, eval=F, echo=T}
ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput(
    "y",
    "Select Measurement of Time",
    choices = c("hour", "dow", "month", "moonphase"),
    selected = "hour"
  ),
  
  plotOutput("plot", width = "700px", height = "500px")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    
    data <- surgery %>%
      filter(!is.na(mort30)) %>%
      mutate(
        hour = round(hour),
        month = factor(month,
                       levels = c("Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun",
                                  "Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec")),
        dow = factor(dow,
                     levels = c("Mon","Tue","Wed","Thu","Fri","Sat","Sun")),
        moonphase = factor(moonphase,
                           levels = c("New Moon", "First Quarter",
                                      "Full Moon", "Last Quarter"))
      ) %>%
      filter(!is.na(.data[[input$y]])) %>%
      group_by(.data[[input$y]]) %>%
      summarize(mortality_rate = mean(mort30 == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE),
                .groups = "drop")
    
    ggplot(data, aes(x = .data[[input$y]], y = mortality_rate)) +
      geom_col(fill = "turquoise4", alpha = 0.8) +
      labs(
        title = paste("Mortality Rate by", input$y),
        x = input$y,
        y = "Mortality Rate"
      ) +
      theme_minimal()
    
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```
